overrides.reason: Original said three markets are at risk and the rest are on or near plan. The status snapshot flags six (2 off track, 4 at risk); UK and France are under forecast.

answer.text: Six markets are flagged in the status snapshot (May 2026, the latest month in the data). Two are off track: Germany, at 92.2% of forecast and down 9.7% year on year after a sharp dip in March, and Spain, which is 4.7% above forecast but down 4.6% year on year. Four are at risk: the United Kingdom (94.6% of forecast), Italy (93.8%), Brazil (95.5%) and France (96.7%). The other seven markets are on track. The data shows what moved, not why.

overrides.reason: Original said actuals 'came in well under forecast for those months, which is what pulled the market into off-track territory'. Germany was already at about 92% of forecast before March (Dec 92.7%, Jan 92.6%, Feb 91.1%) and the March forecast fell with the actuals, so the data does not show the dip as the cause of the status. Only the supported facts are stated.

answer.text: Germany's revenue fell sharply in March 2026 to $1,211,930, down 27.2% from February and 31.0% below the prior year. The drop runs across all five products, each down 29% to 35% year on year in March. Actuals were between 91% and 93% of forecast in every month from December 2025 to May 2026, so the dip is not a new miss against forecast: the March forecast fell along with the actuals. Revenue recovered in April and May but is still 9.7% below the prior year in May. The data shows what fell, not why.

overrides.reason: Original said Europe is hovering just below 100% and blamed only Germany and Italy. Europe is 95.4% (4.6 points under plan) and the UK and France are also under forecast.

answer.text: APAC is outgrowing Europe. APAC revenue is up 11.5% year on year and sits at 104.9% of forecast; Europe is up 1.7% and sits at 95.4%, about 4.6 points under plan. China (106.6% of forecast, up 18.2%) and Japan (104.2%, up 9.7%) lead APAC. In Europe, Germany (92.2%), Italy (93.8%), the United Kingdom (94.6%) and France (96.7%) are all under forecast.

The shortfalls are in specific markets: Germany (−$141,058 versus forecast), the United Kingdom (−$117,597), Italy (−$61,722), France (−$55,492) and Brazil (−$52,249). The data does not break out what drives each market's forecast, so it cannot explain why these markets fell short.

answer.text:
Here's the portfolio at a glance (May 2026, the latest month in the data).

Overall the portfolio is ahead of plan and growing: revenue is $22,850,419, up 7.3% year on year and 100.4% of forecast. APAC and North America carry it. China is the largest market ($3,776,883) and is 6.6% ahead of forecast; the United States ($2,949,131) and Japan ($2,909,296) follow.

APAC is the growth region at +11.5% and 104.9% of forecast. China and Japan are both ahead of plan, and India (+7.0%, 104.2% of forecast) is also ahead. Australia is on plan (101.5%) with modest growth (+2.4%). North America is up 10.2% and at 101.0% of forecast, with the United States and Canada both on plan.

Europe is the soft spot, up 1.7% and at 95.4% of forecast. Germany fell sharply in early 2026, worst in March, and is still 9.7% below the prior year. Italy, the United Kingdom and France are under forecast, and Spain is above forecast but down 4.6% year on year. LATAM is at 98.0% of forecast: Mexico is on plan and Brazil is 4.5% under it.

Six markets carry an at-risk or off-track flag: Germany, Spain, the United Kingdom, Italy, Brazil and France. Ask me about any of them for the detail behind these numbers.
